body:
Today, while mowing the lawn, I came upon a scattered group of salmon-capped shrooms growing in the grass underneath a row of hazels. I would've ordinarily ignored them, but I noticed the tell-tale 'psilocybe' blue stain on some broken caps! Happy that providence had placed (what seemed to be) magic shrooms in my own yard, I collected a few caps and went straight to the computer after finishing the mowing.
For a good half-hour internet I searched online for Psilocybe images that match the (totally) salmon pink caps, yellow spongy gills, reddish-white stems, and bluish stains of the specimens. No match. Not even close! The best match was P. stuntzii, but practically all attributes were off.
I searched elsewhere on Google and eventually came to a nice mushroom identification page that listed pics by type. After clicking 'Boletes,' I found a picture of Boletus pinicola that nearly matched my specimen and seemed to have some faint blue stains on the gills (my research came across references of non-psychoactive shrooms that stain blue, too). On another site I found even better matches with Boletus mirabilis and many other boletes.
Boletes are a diverse group with a large number of edible members, and a few inedible and toxic ones. My shrooms' growth near tree roots is typical for the boletes, so I'm pretty certain that's what they are. Chances are, had I tried tripping on my caps, I would've had nothing more than a funny tasting appetizer. However, it is possible that I could've been poisoned due to the myth that blue staining is a universal sign of psilocybin...
So, if you find a blue staining mushroom, identify it against known species and consume it ONLY if you're dead-sure exactly what species you have.
Peace out and happy tripping!
